newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sets higher goals for exports, investments.
newsitem.headline: Manila sets higher goals for exports, investments.

text.p: The Philippines is projecting a 22 percent growth in export earnings in 1997 and 14.5 percent increase in new investments, Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said on Friday.

He told a news conference that export receipts could reach $25 billion this year, up from an estimated $20.5 billion in 1996, as local industries expand their exports base to include products which used to be marketed only in the domestic market.

"The texture of our exports will continuously change to gradually include products of which were heretofore only domestically marketed," Bautista said. Top export earners are electronic products and garments.
He added that exports would grow by 25 percent in the near-term, outpacing imports whose expansion would be kept at 22 percent every year.
Bautista also said total investments could reach 550 billion pesos this year from 480 billion pesos registered in 1996.

"A review of investment policies, including an incentive programme consistent with market orientation, comparative future advantages and potential, will be undertaken to put into effect the leap-frogging process towards becoming an newly industrialised country," he said.
